A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoCoT2V-Bench and LoCoT2V-Eval research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: V2 reports original evaluations of 13 video generators, human-agreement measurements, ablations, and appendix analyses and visual cases.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and reports evaluations of 17 generators, an evaluator comparison with VBench-Long, and temporal-complexity measurements against StoryEval-Bench.

M1.justification: The prompt-construction pipeline and five-dimensional evaluation framework remain unchanged. Expanded equations describe the existing scene gating, character anchoring, context inheritance, and averaging procedures. Naming evaluation backbones does not establish a model substitution.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds StoryEval-Bench prompts to the temporal-complexity analysis. The original 234-prompt benchmark, 18 themes, three broad categories, and previously compared prompt collections remain. Additional generators do not introduce new video-generation tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 and corresponding appendix comparisons add LongCat-Video, Sora2, Seedance 1.5-Pro, and Kling 3.0 while retaining all 13 earlier generators. New Table 4 also evaluates VBench-Long against the proposed evaluator on four shared human-agreement dimensions, substantially expanding the comparison set.

E3.justification: The new temporal-complexity analysis uses GPT-5 to count events, assess structural indicators, and assign a five-level event-chain score (Appendix D.5). Appendix B.5 specifies disabling audio for added audiovisual generators. Existing frame-rate targets and human-annotation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds a targeted audit of event-level temporal complexity and comparison against VBench-Long's human agreement. Appendix E extends the five existing visual cases with additional generators. Character-removal and HERD-strategy ablations remain; category analyses are reorganized rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain seed 0, three-annotator mean opinion scores, and PLCC/SRCC/KRCC reporting. Neither adds repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Updated correlations do not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Four generators gain overall, category, subdimension, and visual-case results. The expanded Table 2 ranks Sora2 first at 72.13; previous leader LongLive retains 70.56. All original generators' tabulated scores remain unchanged. New Table 4 and Figure 5 add agreement and temporal-complexity outcomes, while Figure 3 changes correlations, including PQ–TVA from 0.12 to 0.07.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 introduces explicit dialogue-history and anchoring notation and equations for previously described attribute, action, and background scores. These restate the existing mathematical procedure. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark and evaluator contributions, human-alignment claim, and central findings about weak fine-grained alignment and identity preservation remain. Updating 13 generators to 17 expands supporting evidence. Professional-use framing elaborates the real-world production motivation already present in v2.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly acknowledges that not every prompt satisfies StoryEval-Bench's temporal-complexity definition and interprets the added comparisons as validation evidence. Section 5.1 now interprets proprietary models' HERD advantages as better expectation fulfillment while retaining LongLive's temporal-quality strength.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code/data release statement and repository link, identifies Qwen3-VL-8B for previously unspecified evaluation roles, and supplies the temporal-audit prompt in D.5. Conversely, B.5 removes the explanation that methods unreliable at 480p use default or recommended settings. These documentation changes do not establish changes to existing runs.

R1.justification: Targeted additions position the benchmark against StoryEval-Bench, strengthen discussion of VBench-Long, and connect HERD dimensions to film narratology, character engagement, aesthetics, and semiotics. Recent generator and cinematic-control references are added. Numerous other bibliography edits update publication details of existing works.

P1.justification: V3 rewrites the FGA explanation, adds professional-use motivation and Section 5.3, converts several numbered subsections to inline headings, and reorganizes Appendix C. Appendix E corrects the mismatched science-fiction prompt to match the existing sci_fi_9 case. Most prose and earlier prompt templates remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 4 and Figure 5, expands result tables and all five case grids, and updates the overview's top-five chart. Existing figures and tables are relocated, and the prompt-statistics caption's left/right descriptions are corrected. The established display formats and overall design remain.

improvement.justification: New Table 4 provides direct validation against VBench-Long, and Figure 5 adds evidence about temporal prompt complexity. Broader generator comparisons, clearer backbone/access information, and the corrected science-fiction case improve usefulness and interpretability. These focused gains outweigh the small reproducibility regression from removing fallback-resolution guidance in B.5; the core method and conclusions remain stable.
